observations: Photo 0: looking down into an open chest freezer interior; metal liner shows frost/ice residue and some staining, interior appears empty.

Photo 1: front view of a white chest freezer with the lid raised; a round badge reads 'Haier Thermocool 2 YEARS WARRANTY' and 'Chlorine Free Compressor'; visible rust/corrosion along the bottom front edge and around a drain plug.
Photo 2: rear view showing the condenser coil, compressor area, a rating/data label (text too small to read), and a power plug; rust is visible at the base near the feet.

claims.evidence: Marketing language; no way to confirm reliability from photos.
No capacity figure or legible nameplate liters value visible in any photo.

claims.claim: Long lasting freezing for up to five... (cut off)
claims.evidence: Claim is incomplete and no cooling demonstration (frost forming, thermometer, running sound) is shown.
This is a manufacturer's original badge, not proof of an active or transferable warranty for a used unit.

risks.proof: A short video of the unit plugged in, running, with frost forming inside or a thermometer showing a low temperature after 30+ minutes.

risks.risk: Visible rust/corrosion at base and drain plug may indicate age, past leakage, or structural weakness
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the rusted areas and the drain plug/seal to assess severity.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a cosmetic/structural defect, lowering value toward scrap-grade comparable

risks.risk: Unknown internal capacity (liters), which affects price tier
risks.proof: Clear photo of the nameplate/rating label on the back showing capacity in liters.
risks.if_unproven: priced using the lowest plausible capacity bracket among comparables

risks.risk: Unknown age and usage history (how long in service, voltage fluctuations, prior repairs)
risks.proof: Seller statement with photo of purchase receipt or any service record.
risks.if_unproven: priced as used/unknown age, no premium applied

proof_requests: Video of the freezer plugged in and running, showing it cooling or frost forming.
Clear close-up photo of the rating/nameplate label on the back, showing capacity in liters and model number.
Close-up photos of the rusted base and drain plug area.
Any receipt or purchase date information.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a used Haier Thermocool chest freezer by its badge, but cooling function is unproven and rust is visible, so it must be priced at worst case (non-working, corroded) using the cheapest scrap-grade comparable up to a generic used deep freezer in the same market.
